subject: Orbit Labs — dedicated capacity sizing follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@orbitlabs.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Orbit Labs — dedicated capacity sizing follow-up and next steps

Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can size Dedicated properly:  

What we heard from your team (please confirm/correct):
- Peak TPS target: ~120 requests per second (spikey traffic windows up to 2–3 min)
- Sustained TPS: ~25–40 req/s during business hours
- Typical prompt token mix: 350 tokens in, ~450 tokens generated (avg ~800 tokens per request); top-end sessions hit ~2,000 tokens
- SLA target: p95 latency < 250ms for single-turn completion (interactive search/chat experience)
- Preferred deployment mode: leaning Dedicated (isolated pool) but may require VPC for compliance once procurement signs off

Sizing questions we need you to confirm to finalize a recommendation:
1) Concurrency per requester: do you expect 1:1 user-to-session concurrency or multiplexed batching across many simultaneous users? (i.e., are there multi-turn sessions that need sticky KV cache?)
2) Percent of traffic that includes long generations (>1k tokens)? Ballpark percent helps us size memory / KV cache
3) Any hard constraints on GPU type? We usually propose H100 for high-throughput + low-latency gen-heavy workloads; A100 (or A10x) can be cost-efficient for lower token-rate profiles
4) Do you need VPC + customer-managed KMS now, or would hosted control plane with Dedicated pools be OK for POC?

I attached our Dedicated sizing worksheet and the demo logs from today — please fill the shaded cells (or send answers inline) and we’ll produce a 2-option sizing: cost-optimized and latency-optimized (GPU mix + pool size + fallback policy).

Proposed next steps:
- You fill the worksheet or reply with answers to the 4 bullets above (by Thu 12/3)
- We schedule a 30 min sizing aligned call next week to walk the model (I’m available Wed/Thu mornings PT)
- Karthik will prepare two SKU proposals (H100-heavy and A100-cost) with estimated monthly run rate and expected p95 latency numbers

Thanks — appreciate the fast cadence.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: orbit-dedicated-sizing-worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
Attachment: demo-logs-20261130.txt (log snippet)

From: Alex Geller <alex.geller@orbitlabs.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@orbitlabs.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Orbit Labs — dedicated capacity sizing follow-up and next steps

Thanks Rishi — quick answers inline. Filling the worksheet today and will send the sheet back by EOD Thursday as requested.

1) Concurrency: multiplexed users. We have ~10k active MAUs, but typical concurrent sessions during peak map to ~200–400 simultaneous open sessions. Most requests are stateless search-like calls; we do have a smaller cohort (~10% of peak) doing multi-turn dialogues that benefit from KV cache affinity.
2) Long generations: ~8–10% of traffic are long generations (>1k tokens), mostly for report/summary features.
3) GPU constraint: procurement will prefer A100 class from a cost standpoint; engineering prefers H100 if the latency numbers are notably better. Open to seeing the two options.
4) VPC/KMS: we will need VPC + customer KMS for production, but POC can run in Redwood Dedicated without VPC. Procurement is cc'd to start basic paperwork.

Also — p95 latency target is aspirational; we care more about consistent <300ms for short (<=512 token) responses.

Alex
Alex Geller
Head of Product Engineering, Orbit Labs
alex.geller@orbitlabs.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@orbitlabs.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Orbit Labs — dedicated capacity sizing follow-up and next steps

Perfect — thanks for the clarifications, Alex. Based on that:
- We'll prepare two explicit configurations:
  A) Latency-optimized (H100-heavy): target p95 < 250ms for <=512 token flows; handle spikes to 400 concurrent sessions with KV affinity for the 10% multi-turn cohort
  B) Cost-optimized (A100-mix): slightly higher p95 (~300ms) for short flows but ~20–30% lower monthly cost; will recommend additional warm cache instances to reduce cold-starts for long generations

Action items:
- Alex / Orbit: return the worksheet with the shaded cells completed (esp. exact avg/95th token counts and concurrent session estimate) — due Thu 12/3
- Redwood (Karthik + Rishi): we will produce a short one-page SKU comparison and a recommended pool config (GPU mix, pool size, burst capacity, fallback routing) by Mon 12/7
- Procurement (cc): we’ll drop a short compliance checklist for VPC/KMS onboarding once POC sizing is confirmed

I attached a calendar link in the worksheet — I’ll hold Wed 12/9 9:00–9:30 AM PT as a tentative sizing call (Alex, let me know if that works).

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
